hints: Focus on what alkaline aqueous iodine is really testing for, the triiodomethane (iodoform) reaction and its yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$.
Recall the two key positive groups: a methyl carbonyl $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ (methyl ketone or ethanal) and a methyl secondary alcohol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ which can be oxidised in situ.
Check each perfume molecule for those exact fragments, remembering that other aldehydes, tertiary alcohols and 1,2-diols without a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ unit do not react.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform test**

Think of alkaline aqueous iodine as a detector for a very specific fragment. A yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ forms only with $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$, or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$.

Test rule:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{C=O or CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-} + \text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3\text{(s, yellow)} + \text{other products}$$

**Examine compound 1**

Compound 1 has a tertiary alcohol $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C(OH)-}$ and an aldehyde $-\text{CHO}$ attached directly to a ring. It is not ethanal, so it is not $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, and it has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ group. So 1 is negative.

**Examine compound 2**

Compound 2 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$, propane-1,2-diol. Look at the left end, it clearly contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$. This secondary alcohol is oxidised by the reagent to a methyl ketone, which then gives iodoform. So 2 is positive.

**Examine compound 3 and conclude**

Compound 3 has a tertiary alcohol at one end and a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ unit at the other end, $\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)CH(OH)CH}_3$. That right-hand end is exactly the oxidisable methyl secondary alcohol fragment. So 3 is positive.

Therefore 2 and 3 only give the yellow precipitate.

options.A: Incorrect. This option includes compound 1 with 2 and 3. Compound 1 has only a non-ethanal aldehyde and a tertiary alcohol, neither of which gives $\text{CHI}_3$, so any combination containing 1 is wrong.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes compound 1 and excludes compound 3. Compound 1 is negative as above, while compound 3 is positive because of its $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ group, so this pairing is wrong.
options.C: Correct. Compounds 2 and 3 both contain the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ group. This is oxidised to $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ under the reaction conditions and then cleaved to give yellow $\text{CHI}_3$. Compound 1 lacks this group and does not react.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes compound 1 only. Students sometimes think any aldehyde gives a positive iodoform test, but only ethanal $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ does. The $\text{-CHO}$ in 1 has no methyl group attached, so no precipitate forms.
